me.colorlight.command.engine_off: The engine has not been initialized yet
me.colorlight.general.enable.tooltip: Enable or disable automatic colored block lighting.
me.colorlight.general.light_range.toolti: Maximum distance that colored light can spread.
me.colorlight.general.smooth_lighting.to: Blends colored light between neighboring blocks at each vertex for a softer appearance. When disabled, each face uses a single sample instead, which is cheaper.
me.colorlight.general.additive_mix.toolt:
On: If two different light sources are positioned close to each other, their overlap will blend smoothly, creating a new color at the point of intersection.

Off: The light will transition more abruptly, without creating any new colors.
me.colorlight.general.tint_gamma.tooltip: Curves how strongly a block's colour shows up, and how far from the light it lasts. 100% is linear: the colour needs strong light to be clearly visible and fades with the brightness. Lower values make the colour stand out sooner, even in dim spots; with the shader lighting, values near 0% also keep the hue fully saturated all the way to the edge of the light. Higher values keep it subtle until a block is nearly saturated.
me.colorlight.general.propagation_mode.t:
Changes how light spreads from standard blocks.
The list comes from JSON files in resource packs (assets/colorlight/propagation); ColorLight ships two: Grid (diamond, vanilla-like, cheapest) and Smooth (circle, 1/8-block precision, costlier). Blocks can name their own method in their block JSON entry. Existing light is recalculated when the setting is changed.
A resource pack may supply its own default for this setting; once you change it here, your choice is kept.
me.colorlight.compatibility.dynamic_prop: How the light of moving sources (e.g. entities with LambDynamicLights) spreads. Only methods defined by a table (not a custom propagate function) can be used; otherwise Smooth is used.
me.colorlight.general.gpu_pipeline.toolt: Lights terrain per pixel in a shader instead of baking colours into chunk meshes. Smoother light, and light changes no longer rebuild chunks. Needs a Sodium version ColorLight supports, otherwise vertex colours are used automatically. Takes effect immediately. Can't be changed while a shader pack is on.
me.colorlight.general.gpu_light_sections: How many 16x16x16 sections of coloured light the shader pipeline keeps on the graphics card at once (16 KiB each). Only sections that actually hold light use a slot. Raise it if light is missing far from you in a big lit area; lower it to save video memory. Applies immediately.
me.colorlight.general.weight.tooltip: Controls how the texture scanner picks each block's light color: every visible pixel is scored by these weights, and the highest-scoring pixel wins.
Favors brighter pixels. Raise it to pick lighter, more vivid-looking colors; lower it to let darker pixels compete on equal footing.
me.colorlight.general.local_weight.toolt: Favors pixels sitting inside a locally bright patch (averaged over the surrounding pixels) rather than a single bright speck. Helps pick the color of a glowing area instead of a stray highlight.
me.colorlight.general.region_weight.tool: Favors colors from large, uniformly colored regions of the texture over tiny isolated dots. Off by default because measuring region size is the most expensive part of the scan.
me.colorlight.general.alpha_weight.toolt: Favors fully opaque pixels over semi-transparent ones, so the scan avoids picking a color from a faded or see-through part of the texture.
me.colorlight.general.anomaly_weight.too: Favors pixels whose color stands out from the texture's average color, such as a glowing ember on an otherwise dark block.
Favors vivid, strongly colored pixels over greys, blacks and whites.
me.colorlight.general.glowcolorscore_wei: Favors pixels that are both bright and saturated at once, the combination that looks like a glow source.
me.colorlight.general.whitepenalty_weigh: Lowers the score of washed-out, near-white pixels (low saturation, high brightness), steering the pick toward colored pixels instead of white highlights.
me.colorlight.compatibility.entity_track: Master switch for scanning entities for glowing blocks LDL. Disable it to turn this feature off completely.
me.colorlight.compatibility.entity_follo: Uses the client's render distance, in chunks, as the radius for scanning entities for glowing blocks LDL. Disable this to use a fixed radius.
me.colorlight.compatibility.entity_check: Radius, in chunks, used to scan entities for glowing blocks LDL. Only used when “Follow render distance” is disabled.
me.colorlight.compatibility.lod_import.v: Reads the world's light sources again from Voxy's saved data, slowly and in the background. The light is found automatically and remembered between sessions (one file shared with Distant Horizons); use this only if something looks wrong.
me.colorlight.compatibility.lod_import.d: Rescan far light from Distant Horizons

Reads the world's light sources again from Distant Horizons' saved data, slowly and in the background. The light is found automatically and remembered between sessions (one file shared with Voxy); use this only if something looks wrong.
Done. %s light sources known. New and changed chunks are added automatically.
me.colorlight.compatibility.voxy_light.t: Colours the light on Voxy's distant terrain. Nothing is read until you press Import below; after that new chunks are added in the background. Needs Voxy.
me.colorlight.compatibility.dh_light: Coloured light on Distant Horizons LODs
me.colorlight.compatibility.dh_light.too: Colours the light on Distant Horizons' distant terrain, read from its own saved data through its public API in the background (reaches as far as Distant Horizons' own data does, not just loaded chunks). A changed light shows up within about 20 seconds. Needs Distant Horizons.
me.colorlight.compatibility.create_contr: Light-emitting blocks on moving Create contraptions become dynamic lights that follow the contraption, so they light the terrain around it and the contraption itself. Nothing is calculated while no contraption is nearby.
me.colorlight.compatibility.sable_cross_: Light between the world and sub-levels

Lights of Sable sub-levels (ships, contraptions) light the terrain around them, and terrain lights close to a sub-level light it. Uses dynamic lights; the terrain-to-sub-level direction needs the GPU pipeline. Nothing is calculated while no sub-level is nearby.
me.colorlight.compatibility.sable_light_: How far, in blocks, the light of a sub-level spreads into the world. It is the same as dimming the light, so it cannot go beyond the general light range; lower values are cheaper.
me.colorlight.compatibility.sable_sublev: Lights of one Sable sub-level also light the other sub-levels they reach (a lamp on one ship lights the ship next to it). Needs the GPU pipeline and "Light between the world and sub-levels".
me.colorlight.compatibility.sable_propag: How the light that crosses between the world and Sable sub-levels, and the light of Create contraptions drawn by Flywheel, spreads. By default it is the same as the moving light method. Only methods defined by a table can be used; otherwise Smooth is used.
